candidates.explanation: Rotation depends entirely on sessionService.updateByHash({id, hash: data.hash}, {hash}) failing when the presented hash is no longer the stored one. The service never checks that the session's current hash equals the token's hash itself. If updateByHash does not filter on the hash, or returns the session anyway, a replayed refresh token succeeds again and a new pair is issued. This is the only place the rotation check happens, because JwtRefreshStrategy.validate only checks that sessionId exists.

I could not see this code, so the line range is a placeholder. The method is probably the real defect: if it updates by id only and ignores the hash condition, it overwrites the hash and returns the session for any stale hash. Rotated refresh tokens would then still be accepted. The same applies to the matching repository update method. Check that the hash is part of the where clause.

validate only checks that payload.sessionId is present. It does not verify the payload hash against the stored session hash, so stale tokens pass the guard. Rejection relies solely on the downstream service check.

fix.description: In refreshToken, load the session with sessionService.findById(data.sessionId). Throw UnauthorizedException if it is missing or if session.hash !== data.hash. Then rotate the hash. Make updateByHash an atomic compare-and-set so the where clause includes both id and the old hash, and it returns null when no row matched.
